Bug_Details: Certain wildcard types can confuse the compiler.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is caused by assigning a List<String> to a List<?> and then attempting to set an integer value at index 0. This compiles without error because the compiler doesn't know the type of the List<?> at runtime, but it will throw a ClassCastException at runtime because the List contains Strings.
Seed_Compilation_Fail_Details:

        wildcardList.set(0, 123); // BUG: UnsafeWildcard - Compiler allows this but it will throw a runtime exception
                            ^

Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered when an integer is assigned to a List<?> which is actually a List<String>. This causes a ClassCastException to be thrown at runtime.
